newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt wins confidence vote on mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt wins confidence vote on mini-budget.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government on Tuesday won a confidence vote in the lower Chamber of Deputies called to speed up approval of its controversial mini-budget.

The government won the vote, its 21st such do-or-die measure in a year, by 318 to 260. Opposition parties had presented hundreds of amendments to the package which is designed to trim the 1997 deficit by 15.5 trillion lire ($9 billion) to qualify for European monetary union in 1999.
The government's victory swept aside the blocking amendments and will allow the bill to pass to the Senate (upper house).
The mini-budget has been slammed by the opposition and even centrists in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition for seeking early payment of taxes by companies on severance payment funds.
The government has cut the amount it plans to raise in this way to five trillion lire from six trillion because of the outcry and intends to raise the rest via tax amnesties.

Prodi has introduced just under 100 trillion lire of belt-tightening measures in the past year to cut the budget deficit to three percent of Gross Domestic Product as required for single currency aspirants. The 1996 ratio was 6.7 percent. ($1=1,706)
